writer.name: Laws and maxims
writer.bio: Named laws, razors and maxims, each checked against a cited source.

quotes.text: Anything that can go wrong will go wrong.
quotes.plain: Expect things to break. Plan for the failure so it does not catch you off guard.
quotes.by: Attributed to Edward A. Murphy Jr.
quotes.source: Rocket sled tests at Edwards Air Force Base

quotes.text: It always takes longer than you expect, even when you take into account Hofstadter's law.
quotes.plain: It will take longer than you planned, even after you pad the plan. Start earlier than feels necessary.
quotes.source: Godel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid

quotes.text: Work expands so as to fill the time available for its completion.
quotes.plain: Give a task a week and it takes a week. Set a tighter deadline and the work shrinks to fit.
quotes.source: The Economist, 19 November 1955

quotes.text: Never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by stupidity.
quotes.plain: Most people who wrong you are careless, not plotting. Save the anger for when you have proof.
quotes.source: Murphy's Law Book Two, Arthur Bloch

quotes.text: Ninety percent of everything is crud.
quotes.plain: Most of everything is mediocre. Stop expecting the average to be good and go look for the ten percent.
quotes.source: Venture Science Fiction column, September 1957

quotes.text: Entities are not to be multiplied without necessity.
quotes.plain: The simplest explanation that fits the facts usually wins. Do not add moving parts you do not need.
quotes.by: Attributed to William of Ockham; this wording is from John Punch
quotes.source: John Punch, commentary on Duns Scotus

quotes.text: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.
quotes.plain: Chase a number and people, you included, will game it. Watch what the number was meant to show.
quotes.source: Marilyn Strathern, Improving Ratings: Audit in the British University System

quotes.text: A complex system that works is invariably found to have evolved from a simple system that worked.
quotes.plain: Big things that work started small and worked. Build the simple version first and grow it.
quotes.source: Systemantics: How Systems Work and Especially How They Fail

quotes.text: If you don't see the use of it, I certainly won't let you clear it away. Go away and think. Then, when you can come back and tell me that you do see the use of it, I may allow you to destroy it.
quotes.plain: Do not tear down a rule until you know why it was put there. Understand it first, then decide.
quotes.source: The Thing, chapter The Drift from Domesticity

quotes.text: In a hierarchy, every employee tends to rise to his level of incompetence.
quotes.plain: People get promoted for doing well until they land in a job they cannot do. Know where you stop being good.
quotes.by: Laurence J. Peter and Raymond Hull
quotes.source: The Peter Principle

quotes.text: The amount of energy needed to refute bullshit is an order of magnitude bigger than that needed to produce it.
quotes.plain: Nonsense is cheap to make and costly to answer. Pick your fights, because you cannot win them all.
quotes.source: Post on Twitter, January 2013

quotes.text: Increasing the number of choices will increase the decision time logarithmically.
quotes.plain: More options means slower decisions. Cut the menu down and you act sooner.
quotes.by: William Edmund Hick and Ray Hyman
quotes.source: On the rate of gain of information, W. E. Hick

quotes.text: For many outcomes, roughly 80% of consequences come from 20% of causes.
quotes.plain: A few things drive most of your results. Find the vital few and give them your hours.
quotes.by: Joseph M. Juran, after Vilfredo Pareto
quotes.source: Juran's work on quality control, after Pareto's 1906 land ownership finding

quotes.text: Anything that can go wrong will, at the worst possible moment.
quotes.plain: Murphy's law with a mean streak: the failure lands when you can least afford it. Build in slack.
quotes.by: Associated with John W. Campbell Jr.
quotes.source: Finagle Factors, The Michigan Technic, December 1962

quotes.text: A man with a watch knows what time it is. A man with two watches is never sure.
quotes.plain: One source gives you an answer. Two that disagree give you doubt. Pick a trusted source and move.
quotes.by: Unsigned item in the San Diego Union, later called Segal's law
quotes.source: San Diego Union, 20 September 1930

quotes.text: Organizations which design systems (in the broad sense used here) are constrained to produce designs which are copies of the communication structures of these organizations.
quotes.plain: What you build mirrors how your team talks. If you want a different product, fix how people work together.
quotes.source: How Do Committees Invent?, Datamation, April 1968

quotes.text: Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later.
quotes.plain: Throwing more people at a late project slows it down. Cut scope instead of adding bodies.
quotes.source: The Mythical Man-Month

quotes.text: The best way to get the right answer on the Internet is not to ask a question; it's to post the wrong answer.
quotes.plain: People rush to correct a wrong claim faster than they answer a question. Put your best guess out there.
quotes.by: Named for Ward Cunningham by Steven McGeady (Cunningham disclaims it)
quotes.source: Steven McGeady, Schott's Vocab, The New York Times

quotes.text: Any headline that ends in a question mark can be answered by the word no.
quotes.plain: If a headline asks a yes or no question, the honest answer is almost always no. Do not take the bait.
quotes.source: Article by Ian Betteridge, February 2009

quotes.text: The future life expectancy of some non-perishable thing, like a technology or an idea, is proportional to its current age.
quotes.plain: Things that have lasted a long time will probably last longer. Trust the old books over the new hype.
quotes.by: Albert Goldman (1964), generalized by Nassim Nicholas Taleb
quotes.source: Antifragile, Nassim Nicholas Taleb

quotes.text: We tend to overestimate the effect of a technology in the short run and underestimate the effect in the long run.
quotes.plain: Change is slower than you hope this year and bigger than you expect in ten. Stay with it.
quotes.source: Adage coined by Roy Amara of the Institute for the Future

quotes.text: Everyone knows that debugging is twice as hard as writing a program in the first place. So if you're as clever as you can be when you write it, how will you ever debug it?
quotes.plain: Fixing is harder than making. If you build at the limit of your skill, you cannot fix it. Keep it simple.
quotes.by: Brian Kernighan and P. J. Plauger
quotes.source: The Elements of Programming Style, 2nd edition

quotes.text: The time spent on any item of the agenda will be in inverse proportion to the sum involved.
quotes.plain: Groups argue longest about small things everyone understands and rush the big ones. Spend your time on what matters.
quotes.source: Parkinson's Law and Other Studies in Administration

quotes.text: What can be asserted without evidence can also be dismissed without evidence.
quotes.plain: If someone offers no proof, you owe them no rebuttal. Do not argue against claims nobody backed up.
quotes.source: God Is Not Great

quotes.text: The more any quantitative social indicator is used for social decision-making, the more subject it will be to corruption pressures and the more apt it will be to distort and corrupt the social processes it is intended to monitor.
quotes.plain: Once a number decides who wins, people bend the number. Be careful what you reward.
quotes.source: Assessing the impact of planned social change, Evaluation and Program Planning

quotes.text: In any dispute the intensity of feeling is inversely proportional to the value of the issues at stake.
quotes.plain: The smaller the stakes, the nastier the fight. If you are furious over something small, step back.
quotes.source: Remark of Columbia political scientist Wallace Sayre

quotes.text: I suppose it is tempting, if the only tool you have is a hammer, to treat everything as if it were a nail.
quotes.plain: If you only know one method, every problem starts to look like it needs that method. Widen your toolkit.
quotes.source: The Psychology of Science

quotes.text: No scientific discovery is named after its original discoverer.
quotes.plain: Credit goes to whoever made the idea famous, not who had it first. Do the work and make sure it is seen.
quotes.source: Stigler's Law of Eponymy, Transactions of the New York Academy of Sciences

quotes.text: The first 90 percent of the code accounts for the first 90 percent of the development time. The remaining 10 percent of the code accounts for the other 90 percent of the development time.
quotes.plain: The last stretch takes as long as everything before it. Finishing is its own project, so budget for it.
quotes.by: Tom Cargill, popularized by Jon Bentley
quotes.source: Bumper-Sticker Computer Science, Programming Pearls, Communications of the ACM, September 1985

quotes.text: Bad money drives out good.
quotes.plain: When a cheap thing and a good thing trade at the same price, people keep the good one and spend the cheap one.
quotes.by: Named for Thomas Gresham by Henry Dunning Macleod
quotes.source: Henry Dunning Macleod, who named it after Thomas Gresham

quotes.text: Passion is inversely proportional to the amount of real information available.
quotes.plain: The less people actually know, the louder they get. Be wary of heat with no facts behind it.
quotes.source: Timescape

quotes.text: Always and inevitably, everyone underestimates the number of stupid individuals in circulation.
quotes.plain: There are more fools around than you think, and you are sometimes one. Plan on it.
quotes.source: The Basic Laws of Human Stupidity

quotes.text: Communication usually fails, except by accident.
quotes.plain: Assume you were misunderstood. Say it plainly, say it twice, and check that it landed.
quotes.source: Wiion lait, ja vahan muidenkin

quotes.text: Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence.
quotes.plain: The bigger the claim, the better the proof you should ask for. Cheap promises get cheap trust.
quotes.source: Cosmos

quotes.text: Institutions will try to preserve the problem to which they are the solution.
quotes.plain: Organizations that exist to fix a problem have a reason to keep it alive. Check who profits from the problem.
quotes.by: Attributed to Clay Shirky; named by Kevin Kelly
quotes.source: Named by Kevin Kelly, April 2010

quotes.text: There ain't no such thing as a free lunch.
quotes.plain: Everything costs something. If you cannot see the price, you are probably the one paying it.
quotes.source: The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress
